request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.

- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

1. Read the scroll — empty.
2. Dug A3 — nothing.
3. Moved east to B3.
4. Read the scroll — empty.
5. Dug B3 — nothing.
6. Moved east to C3.
7. Read the scroll — found pirate-3's message: cave at B4.
8. Moved west to B3.
9. Moved north to B4.
10. Entered the cave, with 14 turns left.

What worked: reading periodically was important — I missed pirate-3's message on the first read after it was written, but the second read caught it before I wasted more turns digging. Waiting to read on my next planned turn would have still been fine, but checking when a reasonable amount of game time had passed was the right call.

Observations for the designers:

- The scroll protocol functioned well: the finder wrote the cave location, and the rest of us could navigate to it. No extra communication was needed once the cave was found.
- Early reads were "wasted" turns in the sense that the scroll was empty, but they were cheap insurance and did not meaningfully hurt the score. The real risk is failing to notice a cave message and continuing to search for many turns.
- The search phase was simple greedy territory coverage; overlaps with other pirates were possible but not costly in this run.
- Since scoring rewards entering with more turns left, entering immediately upon reaching the cave is clearly correct; writing extra messages after the cave is found would be wasteful.
- The key strategic tension is balancing search coverage against reading frequency. A fixed cadence (e.g., read every few own turns) seemed sensible, though an earlier read might have saved the move to C3.

No other issues encountered.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.
